1. The present petition is filed under section 482 Cr.P.C for quashing of FIR bearing no. 0413/2021 dated 20.08.2021 registered under sections 498A/406/34 IPC at P.S. Baba Haridas Nagar along with consequential proceedings.

2. The petitioner no. 1 and the respondent no. 2 got married on 05.12.2011 according to Hindu rites and ceremonies and out of their marriage, one child, namely, Master Jihan Rohila was born on 02.05.2013 who, at present is under the care and custody of the petitioner no. 1.
The petitioner no. 1 and the respondent no. 2 due to matrimonial differences, started to live separately w.e.f. 09.06.2020 without any cohabitation.
3. The respondent no. 2 due to matrimonial differences got registered FIR bearing no. 0413/2021 under sections 498A/406/34 IPC at P.S Baba This is a digitally signed order.

The petitioners no. 2 to 4 are the family members of the petitioner no. 1.

The petitioners and the respondent no. 2 are identified by Investigating Officer, SI Rohit Chahar, P.S. Baba Haridas Nagar as well as by their respective Vivek Rohila & Ors vs Govt Of Nct Delhi & Anr on 13 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170252134/

sentences.text: After conclusion of investigation, the charge sheet was filed and the trial is stated to be pending in the court of Ms. Kritika Jain, South-West District, Dwarka Courts, Delhi/Successor Court.

4. The petitioner no. 1 and the respondent no. 2 have settled their disputes vide Settlement Deed dated 05.12.2022 whereby the petitioner no. 1 and the respondent no. 2 have agreed to dissolve their marriage by way of decree of divorce by mutual consent as per section 13 (B) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

Out of the settlement, the petitioner has agreed to pay Rs.3,00,000/- (Rupees Three Lacs Only) to the respondent no. 2 towards full and final satisfaction of her claims/legal entitlements (past, present and future) arising out of marriage between the petitioner no. 1 and the respondent no. 2 including permanent alimony/maintenance/istridhan, etc. and miscellaneous legal expenses as per the schedule as mentioned in the Settlement.

The petitioner has already paid the entire settled amount i.e. Rs.3,00,000/- to the respondent no. 2, which is acknowledged by the respondent no. 2.
5.

The marriage between the petitioner no. 1 and the respondent no. 2 has already dissolved by way of decree of divorce by mutual consent as per section 13B (2) of Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 in petition bearing HMA no. 1460/2022 titled as Vivek Rohilla and Dimple vide judgment dated 17.12.2022 passed by the court of Sh. Rajesh Gupta, Principal Judge, Family Court, Rohtak, Haryana.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 15/12/2023 at 23:29:20 6.

The counsel for the petitioners stated that as the disputes between the petitioner no. 1 and the respondent no. 2 have already been settled vide Settlement Deed dated 05.12.2022, the terms and conditions of which have already been executed and their marriage has already been dissolved as such, the present petition be allowed and FIR bearing no. 0413/2021 be quashed along with consequential judicial proceedings.

7. The respondent no. 2 stated that she has settled with the petitioner no.1 out of her own free will and without any force, fear or coercion and her marriage with the petitioner no. 1 has already been dissolved.

The respondent no. 2 further stated she has already received the entire settled amount as such, she does not have any objection if the present petition is allowed and FIR bearing no.
0413/2021 along with consequential judicial proceedings is quashed.

8. The Additional Public Prosecutor appearing on behalf of the respondent no. 1 /State stated that under the given facts and circumstances of the case, he does not have any objection if the present petition is allowed and FIR bearing no. 0413/2021 is quashed.
9. The petitioner no. 1 and the respondent no. 2 got married on 05.12.2011 and due to matrimonial differences, they started living separately w.e.f. 09.06.2020 without any cohabitation.

The petitioner no. 1 and the respondent no. 2 have already settled their pending disputes vide Settlement Deed Vivek Rohila & Ors vs Govt Of Nct Delhi & Anr on 13 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170252134/
2 dated 05.12.2022, the terms and conditions of which have already been executed and the respondent no. 2 has already received the entire settled amount.
